record.paper_title: Seven open problems in applied combinatorics
record.original_question: Let G=(V,E) be a graph and let k≥0. A set Z⊂V is an (n−k)-contingent zero-forcing set if it remains a zero-forcing set after deletion of any set of at most k edges. Determine whether there is an efficient algorithm for finding a minimum-size (n−k)-contingent zero-forcing set for graphs with few cycles or, more generally, for sparse graphs with large diameter.

evidence.quote: Definition 7.3 ((n − k)-contingent Zero Forcing). Given a graph G = (V, E), a set Z ⊆ V is a (n − k)-contingent zero-forcing set if for every set of edges E0 of size at most k, Z is a zero-forcing set for G0 = (V, E − E0).
Open Problem 7.2. Is there an efficient algorithm to determine the minimal-sized (n − k)-contingent zero-forcing set for graphs with few cycles? For sparse graphs with large diameter?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let G = (V, E) be a finite simple graph on n = |V| vertices. The zero-forcing color-change rule is: starting from a subset Z ⊆ V whose vertices are colored blue (the others white), repeatedly apply the rule that if a blue vertex u has exactly one white neighbor w, then w becomes blue. A set Z ⊆ V is called a zero-forcing set for G if iteratively applying this rule starting from Z eventually colors all of V blue.

Fix an integer k ≥ 0. A set Z ⊆ V is an (n − k)-contingent zero-forcing set for G if, for every set of edges E₀ ⊆ E with |E₀| ≤ k, the set Z is a zero-forcing set for the edge-deleted graph G − E₀ = (V, E ∖ E₀). Let Z_{(n−k)}(G) denote the minimum cardinality of an (n − k)-contingent zero-forcing set of G.

Question: Does there exist an efficient (polynomial-time) algorithm that, given as input a graph G drawn from one of the following classes, computes Z_{(n−k)}(G) (or a minimum-size (n − k)-contingent zero-forcing set)?
(a) Graphs with few cycles (e.g., graphs G with |E| − |V| + c(G) bounded by a constant, where c(G) is the number of connected components).
(b) More generally, sparse graphs with large diameter.
artifact.status_search_result: A web search for algorithms computing minimum contingent zero-forcing sets on sparse or low-cycle graphs returns general zero-forcing computational literature (IP approaches, Wavefront algorithm, complexity of connected zero forcing) but no result addressing the (n − k)-contingent variant on these graph classes. There is no evidence that an efficient algorithm has been established for this specific problem, so it appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: Computational Approaches for Zero Forcing and Related Problems
status_evidence.snippet: Minimum zero forcing is NP-hard; integer programming and Wavefront-type approaches are used.
status_evidence.claim: State-of-the-art algorithms target standard zero forcing variants, not (n−k)-contingent zero forcing.

status_evidence.title: Zero forcing and its applications - Problem List (AIM)
status_evidence.snippet: Open problem list maintained for the AIM zero forcing workshop.
status_evidence.claim: Contingent zero-forcing algorithmic questions appear in current open-problem collections without resolution.
